_comment: Container-only cluster destinations. Loaded ONLY when ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Compose, which
docker-compose sets for the gateway container (see docs/architecture/phase1-checklist.md, H-1).
WHY THE ENVIRONMENT IS CALLED 'Compose' AND NOT 'Production' - do not 'tidy' this back.
Running the gateway by hand without setting ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT makes .NET default to
Production. If this file were named appsettings.Production.json it would then load on a
developer machine and route every request to compose DNS names such as http://authapi:8080/,
which do not resolve on the host - so every route 502s, with a symptom that looks exactly like
a YARP path-prefix bug. Naming the environment 'Compose' means the accidental default loads
nothing: the gateway falls back to appsettings.json's localhost:700x addresses and simply works.
The trap is removed rather than detected, so there is no guard that can itself misfire.
Why a committed file rather than environment variables: the equivalent would be
name, ten times over, with no validation until a route 502s at runtime. A JSON file is
reviewable in the PR and fails loudly if malformed.
Only Address is overridden. Configuration merges per key, so Routes and per-cluster settings
such as document-cluster's HttpRequest.ActivityTimeout are inherited from appsettings.json.
